concepts.name: Fluid versus solid behaviour
concepts.summary: Recall that a fluid continuously deforms under shear stress and that liquids and gases differ mainly in compressibility and in filling their container.

concepts.name: Density and specific gravity
concepts.summary: Explain density as mass per unit volume and compare fluids using specific gravity.

concepts.name: Pressure as force per area
concepts.summary: Understand pressure as normal force per unit area acting equally in all directions at a point in a static fluid.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic pressure variation
concepts.summary: Explain why pressure increases linearly with depth in a static fluid of constant density.

concepts.name: Gauge and absolute pressure
concepts.summary: Distinguish gauge pressure from absolute pressure and recognise atmospheric pressure as the reference.

concepts.name: Buoyancy and Archimedes' principle
concepts.summary: Understand that a submerged object feels an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

concepts.name: Streamlines and steady flow
concepts.summary: Recall what streamlines show and what steady flow means.

misconceptions.text: Pressure at a point in a fluid acts only downward.
Pressure at depth depends on the container's shape or the total amount of water.
Buoyant force depends on the object's weight rather than the displaced fluid's weight.

concepts.name: Pascal's law and hydraulic systems
concepts.summary: Apply the transmission of pressure changes in an enclosed fluid to calculate forces in hydraulic devices.

concepts.name: Manometer and barometer readings
concepts.summary: Calculate pressure differences from fluid column heights in manometers and barometers.

concepts.name: Flotation and floating equilibrium
concepts.summary: Use buoyancy and density ratios to find the submerged fraction of a floating body.

concepts.name: Continuity equation
concepts.summary: Apply conservation of mass to relate speed and cross-sectional area in incompressible pipe flow.

concepts.name: Volume and mass flow rate
concepts.summary: Compute volumetric and mass flow rates from velocity, area and density.

concepts.name: Bernoulli's equation
concepts.summary: Apply the relation between pressure, speed and height along a streamline for steady, inviscid, incompressible flow.

concepts.name: Viscosity as internal friction
concepts.summary: Explain viscosity as resistance to shear and how it differs between fluids and with temperature.

concepts.name: Laminar versus turbulent flow
concepts.summary: Describe the qualitative difference between smooth layered flow and chaotic mixing flow.

misconceptions.text: Fluid speeds up in a narrowing pipe because pressure must always rise there.
Bernoulli's equation holds between any two points in a fluid regardless of friction or flow type.
Thicker-looking or denser fluids are always more viscous.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic force on surfaces
concepts.summary: Calculate the resultant hydrostatic force and its line of action on plane submerged surfaces.

concepts.name: Reynolds number
concepts.summary: Compute Reynolds number and use it to predict laminar, transitional or turbulent flow in pipes.

concepts.name: Hagen-Poiseuille laminar pipe flow
concepts.summary: Apply the parabolic velocity profile and flow-rate-pressure-drop relation for laminar pipe flow.

concepts.name: Major head loss in pipes
concepts.summary: Calculate frictional head loss using the Darcy-Weisbach equation and friction factor from Moody chart or correlations.

concepts.name: Minor losses in fittings
concepts.summary: Include losses from valves, bends and area changes using loss coefficients.

concepts.name: Extended Bernoulli with pumps and losses
concepts.summary: Analyse a system using the energy equation in head form including pump head, turbine head and losses.

concepts.name: Momentum equation for control volumes
concepts.summary: Analyse forces on bends, nozzles and jets by applying momentum balance to a control volume.

concepts.name: Drag and boundary layer concepts
concepts.summary: Use drag coefficients and distinguish friction drag from pressure drag with the boundary layer idea.

misconceptions.text: Head loss in a pipe is caused by the fluid losing mass or speed rather than by viscous dissipation.
Reynolds number transition at about 2000 is a sharp universal threshold.
The friction factor is a constant of the fluid independent of flow and roughness.

concepts.name: Dimensional analysis and similarity
concepts.summary: Derive dimensionless groups and judge whether model tests are dynamically similar to a prototype.

concepts.name: Pipe network analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse systems of series and parallel pipes and match pump curves to system curves.

concepts.name: Compressible flow fundamentals
concepts.summary: Analyse flows where density changes matter using Mach number, stagnation properties and choking.

concepts.name: Boundary layer separation and stall
concepts.summary: Explain how adverse pressure gradients cause separation and its effect on drag and lift.

concepts.name: Lift and circulation
concepts.summary: Analyse lift on airfoils through circulation and pressure distribution, not simplistic explanations.

concepts.name: Differential continuity and momentum
concepts.summary: Derive and interpret the differential forms of mass and momentum conservation.

concepts.name: Potential flow models
concepts.summary: Evaluate when irrotational ideal-flow solutions using stream function and velocity potential are valid approximations.

concepts.name: Turbulence modelling choices
concepts.summary: Evaluate the suitability of time-averaged turbulence models and wall treatments for a given problem.

misconceptions.text: Lift is explained solely by air needing to travel faster over the longer upper surface to meet at the trailing edge.
Matching geometry alone makes a scale model behave like the prototype.
Potential flow predicts drag on bodies accurately.

concepts.name: Navier-Stokes equations
concepts.summary: Evaluate the terms, assumptions and well-posedness issues of the incompressible and compressible Navier-Stokes equations.

concepts.name: Exact and similarity solutions
concepts.summary: Judge and construct analytical solutions by reducing the Navier-Stokes equations under symmetry assumptions.

concepts.name: Vorticity dynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate flows through vorticity transport, stretching and circulation conservation.

concepts.name: Turbulence energy cascade
concepts.summary: Assess turbulence through energy transfer across scales and the resolution demands it implies.

concepts.name: Choosing simulation fidelity
concepts.summary: Design a simulation strategy balancing DNS, LES and RANS with mesh, numerics and validation.

concepts.name: Stability and transition theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate how perturbations grow and lead to transition in shear flows and boundary layers.

concepts.name: Asymptotic and perturbation methods
concepts.summary: Construct reduced models such as boundary-layer, lubrication and Stokes approximations through scaling arguments.

concepts.name: Flow experiment and model design
concepts.summary: Design experiments or validation campaigns, choosing similarity, instrumentation and uncertainty treatment.

misconceptions.text: Turbulence is random noise unrelated to the deterministic Navier-Stokes equations.
A finer mesh and more computing power always make a CFD result more accurate.
Vorticity is created within the bulk of an inviscid fluid by pressure forces.
